mechanism: Both drugs possess anticholinergic properties; duloxetine has weak anticholinergic effects while oxybutynin is a potent anticholinergic, resulting in additive anticholinergic toxicity and potential CYP1A2 competition.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, cognitive effects); consider alternative anticholinergic-sparing urinary agents or dose adjustment; educate patient on symptom recognition.
